provenance.notes: A 1D transposed convolution with a pointwise large finite weight should preserve subnormal input signal as normal finite output.

skipGpu.reason: Portable WGSL floating-point semantics do not guarantee preservation of the subnormal values required by this fixture. Backend evidence: Metal flushes f32 subnormals to zero (FTZ); subnormal-magnitude values cannot survive the GPU arithmetic path.

provenance.notes: Exercises the neural-audio stride-2 phase decomposition with non-tile-aligned input channels, output channels, positions, and batch > 1.
A phase-tiled neural-audio shape with bias exercises both channel and position tails.
Input-channel, output-channel and position tails exercise transposed convolution at a large output shape.
Compact stride-2 k3 ConvTranspose with bias exercises non-vector channel counts and padded output geometry.
Compact grouped stride-2 fixture that exercises the phase-decomposed nchw2d_grouped_stride_phase fallback on every feature tier.
Grouped stride-2 shape with sixteen output channels per group: the channel-blocked phase route at its full sixteen-accumulator block.
Grouped stride-2 shape with bias and eight output channels per group: the channel-blocked phase route's bias arm at an eight-accumulator block.
f16 grouped stride-2 shape with four output channels per group: the channel-blocked phase route's half-precision storage at a four-accumulator block.
Grouped stride-2 shape whose per-group weight slab (32x64x3x3 f32) exceeds workgroup memory, so the per-pixel phase route rather than the channel-blocked one serves it.
ORT uses the exact output_shape attribute; this fixture has the same natural output size.
ORT uses the exact output_shape attribute; this fixture has the same natural output size.
Covers the exact spatial output_shape [4, 4]; ConvTranspose derives the required symmetric crop.
SAME_UPPER is represented by equivalent explicit symmetric pads plus output padding for this fixture.
Uses the official spatial output_shape attribute from the ONNX backend fixture.
Uses the official kernel_shape, output_shape, and output_padding attributes from the ONNX backend fixture.
Covers one-dimensional ConvTranspose with auto_pad=SAME_UPPER.
Covers one-dimensional ConvTranspose with auto_pad=SAME_LOWER.
Covers two-dimensional stride-2 ConvTranspose with auto_pad=SAME_UPPER.
Covers grouped one-dimensional ConvTranspose.
Grouped (group=2) 1D ConvTranspose WITH bias. Exercises the ncl1d_grouped_bias variant.
Covers one-dimensional ConvTranspose with the optional bias input.
Covers three-dimensional 1x1x1 ConvTranspose with the optional bias input.
SAME_UPPER padding with stride 2. Offset operands keep the scattered contributions proportional to the taps that reach each output position, so a misplaced phase is observable at float16 tolerance.
A stride-two transposed convolution with a four-tap kernel, odd channel and spatial sizes checks padding and reduction tails. Offset operands make a missing tap observable.

Bias on the fused four-phase k4s2 path exercises non-tile-aligned channels and phase-grid dimensions. Offset operands keep each phase accumulation proportional to its tap count rather than cancelling toward zero.
f16 2D ConvTranspose, group 1, IC%32==0 and IH*IW%64==0 -> exercises the im2col-GEMM path nchw2d_gemm (subgroup-matrix) AND the direct nchw2d kernel.
f16 2D ConvTranspose, group 1, IC%32==0 and IH*IW%64==0 -> exercises the im2col-GEMM path nchw2d_gemm_bias (subgroup-matrix) AND the direct nchw2d_bias kernel.
f16 2D ConvTranspose GEMM path with batch=2 — exercises the GEMM workgroup_id.z batching and col2im batch decode.
A zero-depth input leaves a nonempty rank-5 output because the kernel is wider than the empty spatial extent. The contraction is empty, so every output is the additive identity.
Bias is applied after an empty rank-5 contraction, so each nonempty output channel is exactly its bias value without reading X or W.
The empty-reduction fill route also covers grouped rank-4 float16 without allocating or reading an im2col scratch buffer.
A zero-width rank-3 reduction returns one output position per channel containing only the float16 bias.
Covers a non-default depth entry in the exact output_padding list attribute.

Batch 65536 exceeds maxComputeWorkgroupsPerDimension, so gemmDispatchFits is false and every col2im GEMM variant drops out; the scalar NCHW kernel with its bias epilogue is the only remaining f32 dense path.
A batch of 65,536 float16 rows, beyond a single dispatch grid, checks a 1x1 transposed convolution with a single-element bias at default stride 1.
Grouped f16 ConvTranspose at stride 1: the grouped stride-phase kernel requires strideH/strideW >= 2, so unit stride is what routes a grouped f16 request to the scalar grouped NCHW kernel.
A unit-stride grouped float16 input with bias exercises the scalar grouped NCHW bias epilogue because stride-phase handling requires stride at least two.

A rank-5 matrix path with K=32, N=64, and M=32 exercises weight reordering, subgroup-matrix contraction, and three-dimensional col2im. Constant operands make every 2x2x2 overlap multiplicity explicit.

A 3-D pointwise (1x1x1) transposed convolution with 32 input and 32 output channels uses constant inputs (1.0), weights (0.125) and bias (0.5); every output equals exactly 4.5, directly checking the accumulation and bias addition.
A rank-five pointwise transposed convolution with N=8*32*32 and M=32 checks a large spatial extent and three-dimensional tensor indexing.
On the portable register-tiled rank-5 path, bias must be applied in the output-stationary col2im epilogue rather than the intermediate GEMM.

Stride-1 k3 same-size decoder shape on the implicit forward-convolution route: tap-reversed weights, begin pads kernel-1-pad, K=IC*27=216 with a padded tail, and varying operand data so a gather or flip indexing error shows per position.
A zero-pad, stride-one 3D transposed convolution grows each spatial axis and applies channel bias to the output.
Asymmetric begin/end pads give each spatial axis a different forward begin pad (kernel-1-pad per axis), pinning the per-axis pad plumbing of the implicit route.

When kernel size equals stride with no padding, dilation, or output padding, taps tile the output without overlap and col2im uses one source tap per output. The shape follows a factor-4 feature reassembly: x=[1,384,37,49], w=[384,48,4,4].
Kernel == stride on BOTH axes but with different strides per axis (2 x 3), so a kh/kw or inW/outW swap in the collapsed col2im tap cannot cancel out the way it would on a square kernel.
The f16 im2col-GEMM family shares the same col2im shader, so the collapsed tap needs a case on that side of the dtype split too. Shaped after Depth Anything V2's factor-2 reassemble.
For this rank-4 im2col GEMM, gemmM=108 tails a 32-row tile and gemmN=99 tails a 64-column tile. The final materialized-B load must guard the ragged N dimension.
gemmM=16*4*4=256 is tile-aligned while gemmN=5*6=30 is narrower than one column tile, exercising the smallest nonempty N tail on the shared matrix path.
Covers rank-3 f16 ConvTranspose with bias. Exact half-valued inputs keep bias-indexing errors observable without f16 rounding ambiguity.
Covers grouped rank-3 f16 ConvTranspose without bias. Distinct per-group weights 2 and 3 make group-indexing errors observable.
Covers grouped rank-3 f16 ConvTranspose with per-output-channel bias. The two bias entries differ in sign and magnitude, making a wrong channel index observable.

A zero input-depth dimension with a unit kernel produces a zero output-depth dimension. This exercises the direct rank-5 fallback when the GEMM column dimension is zero and the nonempty-output reduction does not apply.
Bias does not make an output tensor with a zero spatial dimension nonempty; the direct rank-5 zero-column path must still produce an empty output.

The phase GEMM must omit those taps instead of multiplying synthetic padding zeros by NaN/Infinity. Batch two and one-row/one-column cases cover phase addressing and degenerate axes.
